newsitem.title: UK: Bass shares down amid OFT concerns.
newsitem.headline: Bass shares down amid OFT concerns.

text.p: Shares in Bass Plc dropped on Monday after a report in the Financial Times said the brewing and hotels group would have to make major concessions to secure regulatory approval for its purchase of Carlsberg-Tetley.
The stock was down 8p at 785 by 0843 GMT in thin volume of 31,037 shares -- extending a decline since it hit a record 850p on August 29, two days after the Carlsberg deal was confirmed.
The FT said Bass may be forced to sell 1,000 of its 4,000 pubs to allay concerns about its market power following the Carlsberg acquisition, with the Office of Fair Trading probing the issue.
Yet analysts said it was no surprise Bass's rivals were pressing the OFT to extract concessions from the company.
"All the others will be looking for the best possible deal," said Dermot Carr, analyst at Nikko Europe.
At Lehman Brothers, analyst Fraser Ramzan said today's FT report contained nothing new to change his neutral stance on the stock.

He said he believed the acquisition would erode shareholder value over the longer-term, with Bass running the risk of losing some of Allied-Lyons Plc's pub supply contracts when they came up for renegotiation.
Ramzan said Bass may emerge with a larger market share but margins in the brewing industry overall were still under pressure from supermarket operators and pub chains.
A spokeswoman for Bass said the company had no comment on the FT report.
